response_geometry: One generated response coordinate is assigned to each of the three modules. Gross shape is exactly 0.6 times preliminary coordinate 0 minus 0.4 times preliminary coordinate 1 plus independent N(0,0.6^2) noise generated with seed plus 700000; its generating environment coefficient is the same 0.6/-0.4 linear transform without a noise coefficient. This pilot validates complete-family assembly and minimally resolves the first Holm threshold; it does not validate the final multicoordinate colour or gross-shape geometry.
family_rule: For every outer dataset and grid, use one paired crossed bootstrap draw for all three modules so cross-module dependence is preserved. Each shared draw must estimate every module; a failed module leaves that planned shared draw failed and is never replaced. Derive each module-process-scale candidate probability from the corresponding one-coordinate module draw distribution, fill all 36 planned slots, then apply the frozen holm_complete_family rule. No missing slot is replaced and no favourable grid is selected.
qualification_boundary: 999 planned draws give plus-one tail resolution 0.001, sufficient to cross the first 0.05/36 Holm threshold but still coarse. Eight outer replicates per scenario cannot estimate FWER or coverage precisely, and one-coordinate synthetic modules do not reproduce final colour/shape dimensionality. This is an executable family-mechanics and tail-resolution pilot only. It cannot authorize empirical trait-environment fitting regardless of outcome. A later adequately replicated calibration using the final module geometry and realized-cohort nuisance/rank support remains required.
